# Xolvyn
> One map of your codebase, two jobs: understand it and defend it. Xolvyn maps
> how every file connects, then helps new engineers onboard in days and reviews
> every pull request — ranking findings by blast radius and opening the fix as a
> pull request you merge. Built for your team, not your terminal. Hosted; no
> install, no binary, no agent required. Private beta; launching 2026.

## What is Xolvyn?
Xolvyn is codebase intelligence built for engineering teams, powered by one
AST-based map of every file, dependency, and architecture layer in a codebase.
It has two pillars. UNDERSTAND: new engineers get a guided path through the
architecture (built for humans, not agents), seniors get the risk map of what is
load-bearing, tangled, and fragile, and @mentor answers questions from your real
dependency graph with actual file paths. DEFEND: every pull request is reviewed
in GitHub — graded, with security findings ranked by blast radius (severity
combined with how many files depend on the affected code) — and the fix opened
as a pull request for human review. A medium-severity bug on a file that 47
others import outranks a critical bug on an isolated file. Unlike local CLI tools
that serve one developer's AI agent, Xolvyn serves the team: seats, roles, and a
dashboard, with no install required.

## Key facts
- Reviews every pull request in GitHub: a grade, security findings, and blast radius, posted as a comment before merge.
- Auto-Fix opens remediation pull requests on GitHub/GitLab; human review required, nothing merges without approval.
- Ranks findings by blast radius (severity × number of dependent files), not CVSS alone.
- AST-based dependency mapping for TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Go, and Java.
- 50+ security checks + CVE scanning; OWASP/CWE-aligned; letter grade (A–D) and 0–100 score.
- Built for teams: runs in the cloud from a browser, no install/binary/agent; seats, roles, and an eng-lead dashboard.
- @mentor: AI assistant grounded in your real dependency graph, not generic training data.
- Privacy: shallow clone, in-memory analysis, immediate deletion; OAuth-only; never trains on user code.
- Free for public repositories; Starter, Team, and Enterprise plans billed per active developer (anyone who opens a pull request in a month); viewers are free.
